chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the visitor of al-Husayn makes his sins a bridge at the door of his house, then crosses them, just as one of you leaves the bridge behind him when he crosses it.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.زَائِرَ: Visitor (specifically in the context of Ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: How does visiting Imam Husayn affect one's sins according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) employs the vivid metaphor of sins as a bridge left behind upon crossing, illustrating the complete erasure of spiritual burdens through the visitation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). This tradition underscores the unique intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia theology, where physical or spiritual pilgrimage serves as a transformative act of divine mercy. The imagery reflects the concept of 'Tawassul' (seeking means), positioning the Imam as the conduit through which sins are traversed and forgiven.
